1 # researchPrime
2 
3 **One sentence:** A careful research engine that checks claims against real evidence and tells you how solid each finding is — not just what sounds right.
4 
5 ## Use this when
6 - You need a serious investigation, not a quick web skim
7 - Stakes are high (a decision, a paper, a product bet) and “sounds plausible” is not enough
8 - You want an honest ladder of confidence: observed, corroborated, claimed, unverified, or refuted
9 
10 ## Do not use this when
11 - You only need a fast factual lookup or a short summary
12 - You’re looking for brainstorming or creative pivots (use Jumper)
13 - You need a build plan or code written (use Crucible → Foreman)
14 
15 ## What you get
16 - A structured research report at three levels (full, executive, agent-ready)
17 - Evidence weighted by how it was checked, with honesty stamps when checks didn’t fully run
18 - Multi-round adversarial review when the host can run the Node engine; a clearly labeled lighter pass otherwise
19 
20 ## What it is not
21 - Not a flattering “agree with the user” brief
22 - Not a code builder or product planner
23 - Not a guarantee of perfect truth — it reports what was verified and what wasn’t
24 
25 ## How to start (human)
26 1. Open researchPrime in Skill Foundry (or ask the agent for a deep research run).
27 2. State the question and what a wrong answer would cost you.
28 3. Approve the research plan when you’re shown it (edit or abort if needed).
29 4. Read the deliverable’s confidence labels before you act on any claim.
30 
31 ## Limits (honest)
32 - Full adversarial verification needs Node available; without it you still get a usable report, stamped that deep verification did not run
33 - It refuses to treat popularity as proof
34 - Long runs take real time; plan for progress updates, not instant answers
35
